## Summary

Verified PSI-102 landed on master (PR #49, merged; the earlier PR #48 was closed with a conflict). Investigated the /auth/sign-in 500 PSI-102's history entry attributed to a `submit-button.tsx` formContext bug. Confirmed via @tanstack/react-form's own source (createFormHook.js) that `formComponents` registered through `createFormHook` (SubmitButton here) are plain components assigned onto the `form` object; `formContext.Provider` is established only inside `<form.AppForm>`, which none of the app's forms used. Reproduced live: before the fix, curling a running dev server's /auth/sign-in returned HTTP 200 but the HTML body carried the `formContext` throw and never rendered the real form (PSI-102 saw a 500 because sign-in also lacked a Suspense boundary around its `useSearchParams()`, matching the exact pattern dashboard/kanban/page.tsx already has to guard against). Fixed both: added `<React.Suspense>` around sign-in's form component, and wrapped the `<form>` in `<form.AppForm>` in all 5 places that call `form.SubmitButton` (sign-in, sign-up, forgot-password, reset-password, invite-user-dialog) -- found by grepping every `SubmitButton` caller, not just the one PSI-102 hit. Re-tested against a live dev server: /auth/sign-in now renders the real form ('Enter your email and password' present, no formContext text). tsc clean, oxlint 0/0, bun test 28/28, next build clean. This unblocks manual browser acceptance for every future card in the calendar -> kanban -> finance pipeline, since all of them sit behind sign-in.
